title: Scotch Eggs
subtitle: Soft-boiled eggs wrapped in sausage meat and fried
excerpt: The British picnic classic done properly: a soft-boiled egg wrapped tightly in well-seasoned sausage meat, coated in breadcrumbs, and deep-fried until the coating is deeply golden and the yolk is still runny when you break it open.

recipe.sourceNotes: The Scotch egg was created in London at Fortnum and Mason in 1738 as a portable snack for wealthy travellers, though similar dishes (like the Mughal nargisi kofta, a hard-boiled egg wrapped in spiced minced meat) predate it. The traditional Scotch egg uses hard-boiled eggs; the contemporary preference for a soft, runny yolk requires precise timing and a well-calibrated oil temperature. The sausage meat is typically from good-quality pork sausages; removing the skin and seasoning the meat well is more important than the particular cut. Mustard mixed into the sausage meat is a common addition. A good Scotch egg has a thin, even layer of sausage meat with no gaps where the egg can cause the coating to split during frying.

content.text: For a runny yolk: boil the eggs for exactly 6 minutes, then transfer immediately to iced water to stop the cooking. The frying oil must be at exactly 170°C; too hot and the sausage meat burns before the egg is heated through. Each Scotch egg fries for 6 to 7 minutes; turn it regularly to ensure even browning.

Bring a pan of water to the boil. Lower the eggs in gently and boil for exactly 6 minutes. Transfer immediately to a bowl of iced water. Peel carefully. Flatten the sausage meat into 4 patties. Season and mix in the mustard.

Place a peeled egg on a sausage meat patty. Wrap the meat around the egg, pressing to seal completely with no gaps. Set up a coating station: flour, beaten egg, then panko. Coat each Scotch egg in flour, beaten egg, and panko in that order.

Heat the oil to 170°C in a deep pan. Fry the Scotch eggs one or two at a time for 6 to 7 minutes, turning regularly, until deeply golden brown. Drain on kitchen paper. Leave to rest for 2 minutes before cutting in half. Serve with mustard.
